## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, and early historical reports on who the companions of the elephant were and when. None is used in this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the leader Abraha, the land of Yemen, and the place they marched against.
- The words sijjil and ababil are rendered plainly or left untranslated; a scholar should decide how the page should word them.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Their plot went astray  (`#their-plot-went-astray`)

Cited ayat: 105:1-5

> **105:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَٰبِ ٱلْفِيلِ
>
> **105:2** أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِى تَضْلِيلٍ
>
> **105:3** وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ
>
> **105:4** تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ مِّن سِجِّيلٍ
>
> **105:5** فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍۭ

### Claims

**c1** (105:1): The ayah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant.

**c2** (105:2): He made their plot go astray.

**c3** (105:3): He sent birds in flocks upon them.

**c4** (105:4): The birds struck them with stones of sijjil.

**c5** (105:5): He made them like chaff that has been eaten.

### One-minute summary

The surah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant, and says He made their plot go astray [c1][c2]. He sent birds in flocks upon them, which struck them with stones, and made them like chaff that has been eaten [c3][c4][c5].

### Complete story

The ayah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant [c1]. He made their plot go astray [c2].

He sent birds in flocks upon them [c3]. The birds struck them with stones of sijjil [c4]. He made them like chaff that has been eaten [c5].

### Deep study

The account is a few short ayat and is built as questions followed by what God did [c1][c2]. The word sijjil is left untranslated here, and the word for flocks is read in more than one way [c3][c4]. The last ayah describes the result with a comparison to chaff that has been eaten [c5].

### Kids mode

The ayat ask if you have seen what the Lord did to the companions of the elephant [c1]. He made their plot go wrong, sent flocks of birds with stones, and made them like eaten chaff [c2][c3][c4][c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show a plot that went astray [c2]. Another is that the account is told as something the hearer is asked to consider [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the companions of the elephant were, where they went, what their plot was, or when this happened; the ayat give only the title and what God did.
- Not established: how many there were, how many elephants, or what became of them beyond the comparison to chaff.
- Not established: what the birds were, how many, or what the stones of sijjil were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the leader, the kingdom he came from, the place he marched against and the year of the event.
